diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a strong upward trend (a net rise of ~16% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The spectrum is close to white noise, so most of the variation is irregular and hard to predict. The series reads as stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (2 points, ~2% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.205), which favours a robust combination.

The series shows low predictability and unstable ranking; a robust median may reduce influence of outliers and correlated errors.
Test a weighted combination with inverse_error weights to see if simple error‑based weighting improves over softmax_neg_error on this low‑predictability, highly correlated series.
I want to test a robust trimmed‑mean over the full pool to see if trimming the extreme correlated errors improves SMAPE for this low‑predictability, unstable ranking series.
I want to try a DBA strategy on the full pool to see if a more robust, data‑driven aggregation beats the weighted inverse_error.
Test a weighted inverse_error over the reduced pool1 to see if narrowing to strong models improves robustness for this low‑predictability, unstable‑ranking series.
Test a weighted aggregation over the small, diverse pool1 using softmax_neg_error weights to see if a data‑driven weighting improves on the current best weighted inverse_error result.

I want to try a weighted aggregation over pool1 but using the w1 weight handle, which may emphasize different models than the previously used inverse_error or softmax_neg_error weights, potentially improving robustness for this low‑predictability, highly correlated series.
The series has low predictability and unstable ranking; a robust median over a small correlated group may reduce influence of noisy models.

The series shows low predictability and unstable ranking; a simple mean over the smaller, more diverse pool1 may provide a robust baseline and explore a different aggregation kind than weighted/median.
test a weighted combination on a larger pool (pool2) with inverse_error to see if adding FT_rf helps performance.

decision.justification: Selected 'median on pool1' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8297. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.205); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.42.
